notes: All 61 source and 99 sink candidates from extraction/sources.csv and extraction/sinks.csv were labeled in 11 batches (S1-S4 sources, K1-K7 sinks); every candidate received exactly one label, keyed by file+line+node+callable.
Dedup: 0 duplicate candidate rows found (dedup key file+line+node+callable); 0 rows removed; no candidate was excluded - all 160 rows appear in entries.

Trust model: CLI/sys.argv/argparse-args rows (S1, 23 rows) are operator-trust (invoker == config author) and labeled none/fp; the attacker-relevant boundaries are manifest/metadata file content, patch files, and git/svn subprocess output.

Sanitizers: ZERO entries - no base-containment check, '..' rejection or equivalent exists anywhere in the dfetch tree (pykwalify validation is type-only per resources/schema.yaml; realpath uses are normalization only; the single relative_to use at manifest.py:274 is display-only and raises uncaught ValueError; basename at metadata.py:131 leaves the directory component unguarded).

Classification candidate (1 row): vcs/git.py:149 sparse-checkout open - literal path argument, but manifest-controlled content channel into git's checkout writes; patch_ng apply root= keyword and git sparse-pattern handling are flagged manual-review points.

No PyVul ground truth, patch diffs, or CVE publications were consulted; CVE_APPLICATION_REPORT.md, PATH_TRAVERSAL_AUDIT_REPORT.md and GITHUB_PRIVATE_VULN_REPORT*.md at the repo root were observed in the directory listing but never opened.

entries.rationale: loaded_yaml['manifest'] is the root-dict read of the parsed manifest - the container from which all project/remote field reads flow (ProjectEntry.from_yaml yamldata[key], Remote.from_yaml). Anchors the manifest-content boundary at AST level so the taint query recalls all fields, including dst/src/patch.

yaml.safe_load(text) is the primary parse boundary of dfetch.yaml: every project field (name/dst/src/patch/url/branch/tag/revision/vcs) enters here. The manifest is attacker-influenced whenever it originates from untrusted repository content: child-manifests are read out of FETCHED destinations (get_childmanifests, manifest.py:263-280, reached from update.py:75-77 / check.py:69-71), and 'dfetch import' writes manifests whose dst values are remote-controlled (vcs/git.py:229, svn.py:46). pykwalify validation (manifest/validate.py against resources/schema.yaml) is type/structure-only: dst is an unrestricted unique str, patch an unrestricted str, src type ANY - no path-content constraint. safe_load is a safe loader against object injection (Pass 6 concern) but has no path-sanitizing effect.
kwargs.get('last_fetch') is a datetime field with no path semantics.
kwargs.get('branch') is a version field feeding Version comparison and VCS commands only, never a file path.
kwargs.get('tag') version field; not a path.
kwargs.get('revision') version field; not a path.
kwargs.get('remote_url') is a URL string (stored and reported); not a local path.

kwargs.get('destination') is where the destination enters Metadata state: via from_project_entry (vcs.py:32-35 -> metadata.py:50-65) it is ProjectEntry.destination = the manifest 'dst' - a fully attacker-controlled path string when the manifest is untrusted; via from_file it is the 'destination' field of the previously written .dfetch_data.yaml (remote-influenced content). self._destination drives Metadata.path (os.path.join/basename/realpath, metadata.py:126-134) -> open read at :70 and open write at :165.
kwargs.get('hash') is a stored digest compared in Metadata.__eq__ / local-change detection; not a path.

kwargs.get('patch') of the metadata FILE is only stored, compared (Metadata.__eq__) and logged - never used as a file path. The patch PATH that reaches patch_ng.fromfile comes from ProjectEntry 'patch' (project.py:248, labeled as source).
Root-dict read ['dfetch'] of the parsed metadata file; same content boundary as the safe_load row at metadata.py:71.

yaml.safe_load(metadata_file) parses .dfetch_data.yaml found inside a fetched destination - a file a malicious fetched repository can ship or modify (dfetch writes it only after a successful fetch of the same path). Current consumers (VCS.on_disk_version/_on_disk_hash, report.py:105) read version/hash; the parsed dict also carries destination/patch fields. Conservative source for this file-content boundary; the manifest-side destination entry is labeled at metadata.py:46.
kwargs.get('revision') version field (git SHA); feeds Version/VCS commands, not paths. Note git.py:84-92 rejects shortened SHAs - version validation, not path validation.
kwargs.get('remote') is a remote NAME used as dict key into the remotes map (manifest.py:97-98); not a path.
kwargs.get('default_remote') is a Remote object reference; not a path.

kwargs.get('src') is the manifest 'src' (subtree/file/glob inside the fetched repo; schema.yaml declares type ANY, and the only content restriction in the whole tree is the svn-side single-'*' check svn.py:227-236 - no '..' or absolute-path rejection). Flows via ProjectEntry.source (project.py:331-333) -> VCS.source -> GitLocalRepo.checkout_version: sparse-checkout content write, os.listdir(src), shutil.move(src + '/' + file, '.') and safe_rmtree(PurePath(src).parts[0]) (vcs/git.py:147-170); and SvnRepo complete_path/file_pattern cleanup (svn.py:191-210). Attacker-controlled path fragment with no validation.

kwargs.get('dst', self._name) is THE manifest destination (defaults to the project name): a fully attacker-controlled path string - absolute paths, '..' components and mixed separators all pass schema validation (schema.yaml: dst type str + unique, no content constraint) and all downstream handling. Trackable chain: ProjectEntry.destination (project.py:335-338) -> VCS.local_path (vcs.py:177-180) -> pathlib.Path(local_path).mkdir(parents=True) (project/git.py:70), safe_rm/safe_rmtree pre-fetch clearing (vcs.py:103-105 -> util.py:28-43), join(local_path, '.git') rmtree (project/git.py:80), dirname(local_path).mkdir + 'svn export <url> <dst>' (svn.py:196-202, 242-246), in_directory chdir (update.py:76), find_non_matching_files/os.remove (svn.py:204-210), Metadata.path open write (metadata.py:126-134, 165). The dominant Pass 1 source.
kwargs.get('url') is a remote URL string; not a local path (remote location).

kwargs.get('patch') is the manifest 'patch' file path (schema.yaml: str, no content constraint). Flows via ProjectEntry.patch (project.py:340-343) -> VCS.update existence check (vcs.py:117) -> patch_ng.fromfile(self.__project.patch) (vcs.py:134) - read/parse of an arbitrary attacker-chosen file path when the manifest is untrusted; patch_set.apply(root=local_path) (vcs.py:138) then writes under the equally unvalidated dst.
kwargs.get('repo-path') is a URL path fragment concatenated into remote_url (project.py:314-318); not a local path.
kwargs.get('branch') version field; not a path.
kwargs.get('tag') version field; not a path.
kwargs.get('vcs') is the vcs type, schema-enum-restricted to git/svn; not a path.

yamldata[key] in ProjectEntry.from_yaml is the per-field manifest value read (loop over ProjectEntryDict.__annotations__ keys, including dst/src/patch) - the AST-level point where each untrusted manifest value enters ProjectEntry construction; complements the safe_load root source for field-level recall.
kwargs.get('default') is the boolean default-remote flag; not a path.
yamldata['name'] in Remote.from_yaml is the remote NAME (dict key into the remotes map and display); not a path.
yamldata['url-base'] is the remote URL base; a URL value, not a local path.
yamldata['default'] at remote.py:96 is a serialization WRITE of the literal True inside Remote.as_yaml() (output direction for dumping); not an input boundary.

os.path.isdir(project.destination) is a stat-only probe whose True branch only decides whether child-manifest discovery runs (check.py:69-71); reads no content and blocks nothing - not a dangerous file access.
os.path.relpath(childmanifest_path, start=dirname(path)) builds a display-only relative path for the recommendation warning (common.py:36-39 -> _make_recommendation); never a file-access path.
dirname of the parent manifest path, the relpath start argument of the same display-only warning.

in_directory(os.path.dirname(path)) - manifest directory; path is a real location walked from the process CWD (find_manifest/get_childmanifests, manifest.py:236-280; util.py:80-84), not an attacker-controlled string; the untrusted manifest CONTENT is anchored at the yaml.safe_load source rows.
os.path.exists(project.destination) existence probe guarding diff generation; stat-only, no containment semantics.

main_project_dir = os.path.dirname(path) used only for repo-type detection (GitLocalRepo(main_project_dir).is_git(), SvnRepo.check_path); path is a real location walked from the process CWD (find_manifest/get_childmanifests, manifest.py:236-280; util.py:80-84), not an attacker-controlled string; the untrusted manifest CONTENT is anchored at the yaml.safe_load source rows.

Internal wrapper parameter carrying patch_name (built as project.name + '.patch', diff.py:114) to open(patch_name, 'w') at diff.py:171. project.name is the manifest 'name' field (or a remote-controlled submodule name after 'dfetch import') - a name containing '../' or '/' yields an out-of-tree write. The f-string construction is invisible to AST extraction (detection.json uncoveredCases), so this summary step is required to connect the name to the open sink.
dirname(path) interpolated into an informational log line only (diff.py:169).

open(patch_name, 'w') - patch file WRITE with manifest-controlled path: patch_name is built from project.name (manifest 'name' field; schema.yaml enforces str+unique but no path content) or from remote-controlled 'git submodule foreach' output via 'dfetch import' (vcs/git.py:229, import_.py:177). A name such as '../evil' writes ../evil.patch outside the manifest directory; execution happens with CWD = manifest dir (diff.py:106). The appended fixed '.patch' suffix limits (but does not prevent) traversal.

in_directory(os.path.dirname(path)) - manifest directory; path is a real location walked from the process CWD (find_manifest/get_childmanifests, manifest.py:236-280; util.py:80-84), not an attacker-controlled string; the untrusted manifest CONTENT is anchored at the yaml.safe_load source rows.
shutil.move(DEFAULT_MANIFEST_NAME, DEFAULT_MANIFEST_NAME + '.backup') - both paths are package constants ('dfetch.yaml'); no attacker-controlled component.

GitLocalRepo.__init__(path) wrapper parameter stores the repo path used by every method via in_directory(self._path) (chdir + git init/fetch/reset writes) and the join(self._path, '.git') probe. Primary call site passes self.local_path = the manifest 'dst' (project/git.py:27); vcs/git.py:236-237 passes join(os.getcwd(), sm_path) with remote-controlled sm_path. Propagates the tainted path into the chdir sink (util.py:52).

checkout_version(src) wrapper parameter carries the manifest 'src' (project/git.py:76-78, ProjectEntry.source) into the sparse-checkout content write (vcs/git.py:149-154), os.listdir(src) (:168), shutil.move(src + '/' + file, '.') (:169) and safe_rmtree(PurePath(src).parts[0]) (:170). 'src' has no path-content validation (schema.yaml type ANY); required step from the 'src' source label to the move/rmtree sinks.

open('.git/info/sparse-checkout', 'a'): the PATH argument is a fixed literal, but the written CONTENT is '/'+src from the manifest 'src' field (vcs/git.py:150-154), and git subsequently materializes files according to those patterns after 'git fetch/reset --hard' (:156-157). Whether a crafted sparse-checkout pattern can place files outside the work tree is decided inside git (not visible in this database). Path argument is not attacker-controlled, so held at classification candidate for human review; the content channel is the concern.
Probe deciding whether the manifest 'src' names a directory or a file (afterwards src = os.path.dirname(src)); stat-only with no guard semantics (accepts any path).

os.path.dirname(src) rewrites the manifest 'src' to its directory before listdir/move/rmtree (vcs/git.py:161-170); propagates the tainted value toward the move/rmtree sinks (a 'src' of ../x/f becomes ../x).

os.listdir(src) enumerates the manifest-'src' subtree; each yielded entry is concatenated into src + '/' + file_to_copy and moved by shutil.move (vcs/git.py:169). Summary step from the tainted 'src' to the move source paths; the enumeration itself performs no dangerous access.

shutil.move(src + '/' + file_to_copy, '.') moves every entry of the manifest-'src' subtree into the checkout root with CWD = the manifest 'dst' (in_directory, vcs/git.py:142). The source path is built by string concatenation from the unvalidated 'src' (schema.yaml type ANY), so src = '../outside' relocates files from outside the fetched repository into the destination - a genuine arbitrary-location file move; the destination '.' is CWD-bounded, but CWD itself was set from the same tainted dst family.

PurePath(src).parts[0] extracts the FIRST path component of the manifest 'src' and passes it to safe_rmtree (vcs/git.py:170 -> util.py:36-39 shutil.rmtree). Step needed to connect the 'src' source to the rmtree sink.
pathlib.PurePath(src) construction feeding .parts[0] -> safe_rmtree; same first-component-deletion semantics as the parts row; propagates the manifest 'src' into the rmtree sink.

pathlib.Path(self.local_path) construction immediately consumed by .mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) - the object-conversion step from the manifest 'dst' string to the directory-creation sink.
